name: GNU General Public License version 1
summary: The GNU GPL provided reusable terms intended to preserve recipients’ rights to share and modify covered programs.
description: A reusable free-software copyright license, an institutional and legal arrangement setting conditions for copying, modification and redistribution of covered programs; it is not executable software.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source for this event, not necessarily first preceding work.

events.statement: The Free Software Foundation’s GNU General Public License version 1 text is dated February 1989.

evidence.supports: The license text states its date, scope, copying rights and source and redistribution conditions.

events.caveats: The date printed on the license does not by itself establish its publication day or when a particular program adopted it.

contributions.resource: Held copyright in the license text; rights in covered software belonged to its respective copyright holders.

evidence.supports: The license identifies the Free Software Foundation as copyright holder of the license text.

earliest_record.rationale: The license text bears the date February 1989; the first publication or adoption date is not independently established.

caveats: This is the first general GPL version, not a claim that free-software licensing or copyleft began in 1989. The license does not establish distribution at zero monetary cost.

research.note: Independent reader checked the license heading, preamble, terms 0–3 and the source-code and fee qualifications; this is a legal instrument, distinct from software capability. Later event and measure enrichment has not yet received independent review.
